hypotheses.justification: The theorem also takes `i : Fin d`, and `Fin.pos i : 0 < d` (Init/Data/Fin/Basic.lean) derives the same fact. When d = 0 the type Fin 0 is empty, so the statement holds vacuously. The proof only uses `dimension` to get `(d:ℝ) ≠ 0` and for `positivity`; adding `have dimension := Fin.pos i` at the start leaves the rest of the proof unchanged.

Case N = 0. The lemma `dSVUniformDensityThresholdRaw_norm_sq` (no hypotheses) gives ‖raw‖² = d·0 = 0, so ‖raw‖ = 0. Its inverse is 0⁻¹ = 0, so the left side is 0. On the right, `dSVDensityRationalPhysicalAcceptedRank_gridPrefix` (no hypotheses) rewrites the grid prefix as r/0 = 0, so the right side is √(w·0) = 0. Both sides are 0. Case N > 0: use the original proof. So `grid` is not needed; the proof just splits on whether N = 0.

Case w ≤ 0. We have d ≥ 0, so w·d ≤ 0 and `Real.sqrt_eq_zero'` gives √(w·d) = 0; the left side is 0. On the right, unfold `dSVDensityRationalCanonicalAcceptedCoefficient` (= √(w * gridPrefix …)). The rank lemma `dSVDensityRationalPhysicalAcceptedRank_gridPrefix` (no hypotheses) rewrites the grid prefix as r/N, which is ≥ 0 because r ≥ 0 and N ≥ 0 as reals. So w·(r/N) ≤ 0 and the right side is also 0. Case w > 0: use the original proof, which needs `width` only through `..._targetCoefficient_sq`. So `width` can be removed by splitting on the sign of w. Each of the three hypotheses (`dimension`, `grid`, `width`) can be removed on its own, and the same case analyses also work with all of them removed together.
